reviews.quote: Lightweight with power and 20 hours of endurance. Pros: extremely lightweight and portable design, high-quality IPS display, Wi-Fi 7 and Thunderbolt 4, long runtimes. Cons: slight thermal throttling under extreme load, case is slightly bendy, Intel Arc 140V can't completely keep up with predecessor's RTX 3050.

praises: 1.19 kg for a 16-inch laptop — repeatedly cited as the reason buyers switch from XPS/Legion Ion 16x
Wi-Fi 7 and Copilot+ NPU on the 2025 Arrow Lake board
Port set survives the thin chassis: HDMI, USB-A, microSD and dual TB4 all present
Bright sharp 16:10 touch panel with good colour for office and media
All-day battery for commute/work-day use despite the size
complaints: Lid and keyboard-deck flex noticeably for a $3.5k-class machine; hinge wobble when typing
Downward-firing speakers are thin and easily muffled on a lap or desk
RAM is soldered and storage is the only real upgrade path
LG Vantage bloat and erratic driver/firmware update cadence
Glossy touch panel reflects badly in bright rooms; some units show backlight bleed

design_philosophy: The gram line exists to make big screens nearly weightless, using magnesium-nano-carbon chassis that undercut every 16-inch rival by half a kilogram or more. The 2025 gram Pro adds Arrow Lake silicon, Wi-Fi 7 and a higher-refresh touch panel while keeping the sub-1.2 kg trick. This iGPU tier trades discrete graphics for maximum battery and silence — the 'Pro' badge here means premium thin-and-light, not workstation.
